Shyam Sunder travelled to yet another tribal heartland of Jharkhand to witness a sacred Adivasi puja performed atop a hill revered by the Munda community. During his visit, he met tribal elders and wisemen who opened up about a painful perception — that many in the mainstream society still see them as “Rakshas” (Demon), a stigma they continue to battle even today.
In the midst of these conversations, Shyam also observed a growing tension between tribal groups and the Kudmi community, which has intensified following the Kudmi demand for Scheduled Tribe status. This deepening fault line is reshaping the region's social dynamics.
At the foothills of the holy Marang Buru, Shyam witnessed the Launda Nach at a local mela. This colourful, raw, and energetic performance reflects the cultural pulse of rural Jharkhand.
Through this journey, he brings you close to the lived realities, beliefs, and struggles of Adivasi communities — beyond stereotypes, beyond misunderstandings.
Watch the full story to understand Jharkhand’s tribal world from the ground.
